title: The direct sum of two quasi-coherent modules is quasi-coherent
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $\mathcal F_1,\mathcal F_2$ be quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-modules [pqf-def-coherent], [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $\mathcal F_1\oplus\mathcal F_2$ be the $\mathcal O_X$-module $W\mapsto\mathcal F_1(W)\oplus\mathcal F_2(W)$ (for $W\subseteq X$ open), with componentwise $\mathcal O_X(W)$-module structure and componentwise restriction maps; it is a sheaf, and together with the inclusions and projections of the two summands it is a direct sum (biproduct [def-weil-additive-category]) of $\mathcal F_1$ and $\mathcal F_2$ in $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$. Then $\mathcal F_1\oplus\mathcal F_2$ is a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module.

proof.text: Use the already proved source-library declaration AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.isQuasicoherent_sigma in WeilConjectures.AlgebraicGeometry.Modules.QuasicoherentKernel for the family indexed by ULift Bool with values F1 and F2. The two hypotheses supply quasi-coherence of each value. Construct the isomorphism from the binary biproduct to this coproduct: its forward map is biprod.desc of the two coproduct inclusions, and its inverse is Sigma.desc of the two biproduct inclusions. The composites are identities by biprod.hom_ext' and Sigma.hom_ext, checking false and true separately with the inclusion/desc identities. Transport quasi-coherence along the inverse isomorphism using the isomorphism-closed object property SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent. This argument applies also to the empty scheme.
